text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- State-owned oil company Statoil is offering employees to borrow a PC for use at home if they commit themselves to joining a training project for two to three years in their spare time to become computer literate. Statoil has 14,000 employees.

- The International Atomic Energy Agency has asked Norwegian authorities to analyse the effects of the French nuclear tests at the Mururoa atoll. The state protection agency will analyse samples from Mururoa for signs of nuclear pollution.

- Metal producer Elkem ASA blamed weak demand for ferrochrome and aluminium for a 48 percent slump in operating profits in the third quarter compared with the second. In addition Elkem said that a shortfall in captive power production had added 80 million crowns to the group's expenses for the first nine months of 1996.

- Due to strong growth in the cruise line between Oslo and Kiel, shipping Color Line ASA booked 231 million crowns in pre-tax profit for the first nine months of 1996, which is 50 percent more than during the same period last year.
